entries.note: Quote verbatim in PharmR (bundle); studies reviewed under IND 107475 July 19, 2011, so 2011 proxy holds. No human GI-transit study found for naldemedine (phase 1 HV paper PMID 28960888 is PK/safety only). Judgement that SBM is efficacy, not engagement, is defensible.

entries.rule: Dose table: model stated a tolerability margin
entries.note: Tail-flick (>=10 mg/kg) and post-op pain (>=5 mg/kg) studies are copied from the July 2011 IND review, so the window predates phase 3. Rat ED50 0.02-0.23 mg/kg for transit stated in same review.

entries.rule: Decision 16: stated tolerability margin that held is same with margin_stated
entries.note: SumR quote verbatim. MedR 8.5.2 says a small percentage had increased pain and few needed intervention; margin held overall. Could carry source_calls_it 'partial' but status same stands. Window is two in-rat numbers, not human mg/kg arithmetic.
Quote verbatim in PharmR; castor-oil diarrhoea ED50 0.01 mg/kg also stated. Opening untested at 2011 is correct.

DOI resolves to Hale 2017 Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol (PMID 28576452, epub 2017-05-30); quote verbatim in abstract; primary = responder rate. NCT01965158/NCT01993940 results posted 2017-05-30; NCT01207427 is ADL5945 (bevenopran) phase 2, a member drug.
Quote verbatim in PharmR; teeth chattering at >=3 mg/kg confirmed as only central sign. Study from IND review.

Label quote verbatim (Highlights). MedR 8.5.1 notes PAMORA GI reactions are among the commonest opiate-withdrawal symptoms, supporting the pairing of rat peripheral withdrawal with patient GI ARs. Abdominal pain 8% vs 2%, diarrhoea 7% vs 2% in MedR/CrossR.
Armstrong 2013 (PMID 23512167, epub 2013-03-13) quote verbatim in abstract. Model run before phase 1 (Jan 2010), so 2010 proxy opening untested is right; prospective, not retro.

entries.rule: Year is the later of model source and patient result public; earlier paired source dates the comparison
entries.note: Field year: 2019 -> 2013. Vickery 2013 DDW abstract 899 (doi 10.1016/S0016-5085(13)60574-0) read: primary CSBM wks 2-5, 0.8 placebo vs 2.5/2.6/1.5 (all p<0.05); conclusion quote verbatim. Paired with Armstrong 2013; same, primary. Supplement-abstract admissibility open. | superseded: confirmed (CHECKER_BRIEF / models): Long 2019 full text (PMC6912869): rat loperamide GE ID50 0.24 mg/kg and phase 2b CSBM p=0.0001 stated together. Registry primary is weeks 2-5, paper gives week 5; same holds. Model predates trial, so not retro.
entries.adjudication_note: Primary CSBM responded as predicted; same either way. RULE QUESTION: is the DDW 2013 Gastroenterology supplement abstract tier 1 (rule 2), moving rule 6 year from 2019 to 2013?

entries.note: Quote verbatim in Long 2019 full text (mouse transit ID50 0.35, GE 0.087 mg/kg for 19i). Lead-optimisation screen predates phase 1. confidence_note wrongly cites Armstrong 2013 abstract; source is Long 2019 full text.
Same Long 2019 passage as efficacy 4; mouse screen and phase 2b outcome stated side by side; same, primary, prospective.
Armstrong 2013 abstract quote verbatim; Long 2019 gives no withdrawal at 30 mg/kg in dependent mice. Opening untested at 2010 proxy fine.

entries.rule: Year is the later of model source and patient result public; earlier paired source dates the comparison
entries.note: Field year: 2019 -> 2013. J Pain 2013 abstract 421 DOI resolves (title: no CNS opioid withdrawal for TD-1211, body paywalled); DDW 2013 abstract 899 verbatim: 'no evidence of CNS opioid withdrawal'. With Armstrong 2013 model, same at 2013. Hinges on supplement-abstract rule question. | superseded: confirmed (CHECKER_BRIEF / models): Long 2019 quote verbatim; similar TEAEs is indirect for CNS withdrawal, so partial is right. A J Pain 2013 phase 2b abstract reports COWS max 7 vs 6 placebo (direct withdrawal readout, earlier paired 2013 source); see missing.
entries.adjudication_note: Status same either way (model silence on CNS withdrawal held). RULE QUESTION: is a journal-supplement conference abstract a tier 1 source under rule 2, so rule 6 dates this to 2013 rather than 2019?

entries.note: Armstrong 2013 abstract verbatim: TD-1211 did not inhibit morphine antinociception in rat/dog hot plate; Long 2019 gives >60 mg/kg rat and 3 mg/kg dog vs GE ID50 0.24. Untested opening fine.

entries.rule: Year is the later of model source and patient result public; earlier paired source dates the comparison
entries.note: Field year: 2019 -> 2013. DDW 2013 abstract 899 (Gastroenterology suppl, May 2013) verbatim: 'no evidence of ... analgesic interference'; J Pain 2013 abstract title says same. Armstrong 2013 hot-plate margin public Mar 2013. margin_stated timing rule question still open. | superseded: confirmed (CHECKER_BRIEF / models): Long 2019 quote verbatim (no impact on opioid analgesic use at efficacious doses). Margin first public in Armstrong 2013, after the phase 2b ended (May 2012); see rule question on margin_stated timing.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 16 same, margin held. RULE QUESTION: is a supplement abstract tier 1 for rule 6 dating (2013 vs 2019), and must margin_stated be public before the trial?

missing: Axelopran (member) has a model source the draft says it lacks: Armstrong et al. 2013, Naunyn-Schmiedeberg's Arch Pharmacol, PMID 23512167 (doi 10.1007/s00210-013-0844-5), rat loperamide-inhibited gastric emptying, castor-oil diarrhoea and dog GI contractility plus CNS models; pair with axelopran phase 2 OIC trials (registry/press, not verified here). Likely a separate track (loperamide gastric-emptying model) or same-direction add to the rat transit track; would not change the status but may add an earlier year.

NCT01122030: naldemedine phase 2 in opioid-dependent chronic-pain patients (single doses; results posted 2017-05-30), a human withdrawal/central-effect comparison for the rat withdrawal and analgesia-window tracks; not cited in safety or dose.
PharmR lists a rat in-vivo brain opioid receptor occupancy study (S-297995-EB-257-N) supporting peripheral restriction; a possible separate dose/central-sparing model, not tracked.

Patient side for the mouse withdrawal (safety) and hot-plate window (dose) tracks: J Pain 2013;14(4 Suppl) abstract 'No evidence of analgesic interference or CNS opioid withdrawal for TD-1211 in a phase 2b study in OIC' (https://www.jpain.org/article/S1526-5900(13)00698-6/fulltext; COWS max 7.0 TD-1211 vs 6.0 placebo, seen in search snippet only). Paired with Armstrong 2013 it would date both tracks' same to 2013 if a supplement abstract is admissible tier 1.

Axelopran phase 2b efficacy was public in Oct 2012 (ACG 2012, Am J Gastroenterol suppl; MedPage Today coverage https://www.medpagetoday.com/meetingcoverage/acg/35542; Theravance topline PR). Paired with Armstrong 2013 this gives a 2013 comparison for the rat loperamide GE track, earlier than Long 2019.
rule_questions: Engagement: when the model's PD readout is GI transit and humans measured bowel-movement frequency (the efficacy endpoint), does SBM count as a downstream engagement readout, or must engagement stay untested/not_measured?
Dose: does a central-vs-peripheral window built from two in-rat dose thresholds (no human exposure translation) count as a 'stated tolerability margin' under Decision 16?

Axelopran hot-plate window (dose 4): the margin was generated before phase 1 but first published (Armstrong, Mar 2013) after the phase 2b ended (May 2012). Does margin_stated require a public model source before the trial, or does an IND-era study published later count?
Are conference abstracts in journal supplements (J Pain, Am J Gastroenterol) tier 1 sources for dating a paired comparison?
